extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and practitioners filing PCT (international) applications and entering the U.S. national stage
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/fee requirements for international (PCT) patent applications: determination of unity, international preliminary examination (Demand, conduct, amendments, fees, protests), and requirements/fees/deadlines for entering the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention — categories and combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may claim inventions in categories such as (1) a product, (2) a process for obtaining the product, (3) an apparatus or means specially designed for carrying out the process, or combinations thereof (e.g., product + process, product + apparatus + process specially adapted for manufacture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims contain claims to more or less than one of the combinations set forth, unity of invention might not be present. The determination whether a group of inventions forms a single general inventive concept shall be made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim. When multiple products/processes/uses are claimed, the first invention of the category first mentioned in the claims and the first recited invention of each other related category will be considered the main invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of unity before the International Searching Authority (ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before establishing the international search report, the ISA will determine whether the international application complies with the requirement of unity of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ISA considers the application lacks unity it shall inform the applicant and invite payment of additional fees (PCT Rule 40). The applicant is given a time period in accordance with PCT Rule 40.3 to pay additional fees. If no additional fees are paid, the international search will be performed only on the invention first mentioned (“main invention”) in the claims. Lack of unity may be evident before or after considering prior art (e.g., a discovered document may show a linking claim lacks novelty or is clearly obvious), in which case ISA may raise lack-of-unity objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure against ISA lack-of-unity finding
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant disagrees with ISA's holding of lack of unity, additional fees may be paid under protest, accompanied by a request for refund and a statement of reasons for disagreement or why fees are excessive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The protest will be examined by the Director or designee; if justified all or part of the additional fees will be refunded. Applicant may request that a copy of the protest and decision accompany the international search report when forwarded to Designated Offices (notify ISA prior to issuance of the ISR; thereafter notify International Bureau).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for international preliminary examination (form and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper Demand must be filed on the standardized form (PCT Rule 53) and the preliminary examination and handling fees must be paid within the applicable time limit set in PCT Rule 57.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal of a proper Demand prior to start of IPE will entitle applicant to refund of the preliminary examination fee minus the transmittal fee. Filing a Demand constitutes election of all Contracting States designated and bound by Chapter II of the Treaty as of the international filing date. Any Demand filed after applicable time limits (PCT Rule 54 bis.1(a)) is considered as not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment timing and late-payment consequences for IPE fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling and preliminary examination fees are due within the time period set in PCT Rule 57.3; the fee amounts in effect on date of payment apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees are not paid within the time period, applicant will be notified and given one month to pay deficient fees plus a late payment fee equal to the greater of: (i) 50% of the deficient fees (but not exceeding amount equal to double the handling fee), or (ii) an amount equal to the handling fee (PCT Rule 58 bis.2). The one-month time limit may not be extended. Failure to timely pay will result in the Demand being considered not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: International preliminary examination fees and entity-based rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination fees, additional preliminary examination fees (per additional invention), handling fee, and late furnishing fees (e.g., for sequence listings) are established by the Director and vary by entity status (micro, small, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific fee amounts are set in tables (e.g., $141/$282/$705 for preliminary exam fee by micro/small/other if US ISA was used; different amounts if another ISA was used). Additional per-invention fees follow similar entity-based rates. Handling fee is due on filing the Demand as prescribed in PCT Rule 57. Late furnishing fee for sequence listing in response to PCT Rule 13ter invitations is specified by entity class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and conduct of international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: IPE is conducted to formulate a non-binding opinion on whether claimed invention has novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPE begins per PCT Rule 69.1. No IPE will be conducted on inventions not previously searched by an ISA. IPEA will establish a written opinion if any defect exists or if claimed invention lacks novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability and will set a non-extendable time limit for applicant reply. The written opinion by the ISA under PCT Rule 43bis.1 is considered a written opinion of the US IPEA. IPEA may establish further written opinions. After any written opinion and reply or expiration of reply time, an international preliminary examination report (IPER) will be established and copies provided to the International Bureau and applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews during international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is permitted a personal or telephone interview with the examiner during the period between establishment of the written opinion and the IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be requested after filing a Demand and must be conducted during the period between the written opinion and the establishment of the IPER. Additional interviews may be held at examiner discretion if helpful. A summary of any such interview must be filed by the applicant or, if not, made of record by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may make amendments at filing of the Demand or within the time limit set by the IPEA for reply to any notification or written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such amendments must be made in accordance with PCT Rule 66.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of unity before the IPEA and options on lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing any written opinion or IPER, the IPEA will determine unity of invention. If IPEA finds lack of unity it may (1) issue opinion/IPER indicating lack of unity without inviting restriction or additional fees (no IPE on inventions not previously searched), (2) invite applicant to restrict claims or pay additional fees within a non-extendable time limit, or (3) if applicant fails to restrict/pay, issue an opinion/IPER on the main invention and indicate facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If doubt exists as to which invention is main, the invention first mentioned in the claims and previously searched by an ISA shall be considered the main invention. Lack of unity may be evident before or after consideration of prior art (e.g., discovery of a document showing generic/linking claim lacks novelty or is obvious).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure against IPEA lack-of-unity finding
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant disagrees with IPEA's lack-of-unity holding, additional fees may be paid under protest with a request for refund and reasons for disagreement or that fees are excessive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests are examined by the Director or designee and if justified, additional fees or portion will be refunded. Applicant may request that a copy of the protest and decision accompany the IPER when forwarded to Elected Offices (notify IPEA prior to IPER issuance; thereafter notify International Bureau).

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage commencement, entry, and fulfillment
rubrics_metrics.description: The national stage commences with expiration of the applicable PCT time limits (Article 22(1)/(2) or Article 39(1)(a)). An international application enters the national stage when the applicant files documents and fees required by 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1) and (c)(2) within the period set in § 1.495. The national stage fulfills 35 U.S.C. 371 when commenced and all applicable requirements are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor notes specify different rules applicable to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 363 on or after Sept. 16, 2012. Compliance with § 1.495 timing is required to prevent abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage fees: basic, search, examination, excess-claim and other surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: A schedule of fees applies to international applications entering the U.S. national stage: basic national fee, search fee (varies depending on prior ISA/IPER findings and which ISA performed search), examination fee, excess claim fees (per independent claim over 3; per claim over 20), multiple dependent claim fee, application size fee, surcharge for late payments, fee for late English translations, and fees for additional pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables specify amounts by entity status (micro/small/other). If fees for excess claims or multiple dependent claims are not paid with the basic national fee or on later presentation, they must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the Office-set time period in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment. Surcharge applies when filing the search/exam fee or oath after national stage commencement. Application size fees are imposed for specifications/drawings exceeding thresholds (and per additional 50 sheets or fraction). Specific conditional zero-fee situations exist where an IPER or ISA written opinion states criteria of novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability have been satisfied for all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and timing to enter the U.S. national stage (§ 1.495): 30‑month rule and omitted items procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must fulfill 35 U.S.C. 371 within the time periods set in § 1.495; the thirty‑month time period (and listed subparagraphs) may not be extended. To avoid abandonment, the applicant must, no later than 30 months from the priority date, furnish a copy of the international application (unless already supplied) and pay the basic national fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant complies with paragraph (b) before expiration of 30 months but has omitted required items (translation to English if necessary, inventor’s oath/declaration, search fee, examination fee, application size fee), the Office will notify the applicant and set a time period within which omitted items must be provided to avoid abandonment. The inventor’s oath/declaration may be postponed until application is otherwise in condition for allowance under specified conditions if an ADS identifying inventors and contact info is filed timely. Payment of processing fee is required for acceptance of an English translation later than 30 months; surcharge is required for late acceptance of certain fees or oaths after national stage commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and sequence listing rules for national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations and translated annexes/amendments must be furnished by the 30‑month deadline; sequence listing translation requirements differ by international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A translation into English of PCT Article 19 claim amendments and any annexes to an international preliminary examination report must be furnished not later than 30 months from the priority date; otherwise such amendments/annexes are considered canceled (except annex translations may be submitted later with processing fee). For international filing dates before July 1, 2022, a sequence listing need not be translated if PCT Rule 12.1(d) & PCT Rule 5.2(b) conditions met. For filing dates on or after July 1, 2022, an English translation is required for any Sequence Listing XML containing non‑English language values for any language‑dependent free text qualifiers (see §§ 1.831–1.834). Verification of translations may be required when filed if considered necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and treatment of submissions as national stage entry; abandonment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and fees submitted must be identified as a submission to enter the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. If requirements of paragraph (b) (e.g., copy of application and basic fee) are not complied with within 30 months from the priority date, the international application becomes abandoned as to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents/fees contain conflicting indications between a filing under 35 U.S.C. 111 and a national-stage entry under 371, they will be treated as a national-stage entry. Failure to timely provide required items or fees (without meeting the Office's subsequent notices and windows) leads to abandonment as to the U.S.
